newsitem.title: UK: Sears firmer in heavy volume pre-results.
newsitem.headline: Sears firmer in heavy volume pre-results.

text.p: Shares in Sears Plc nudged ahead on Monday amid heavy turnover ahead of full-year figures due later this week, dealers said
Sears' shares were up one pence, or 1.31 percent, to 77.5p by 1115 GMT in volume of 7.2 million while the FTSE-100 index was 8.8 points, or 0.20 percent, higher at 4378.5.
The group's embattled chief executive Liam Strong put restructuring plans to the board last Thursday, including rationalisation of loss-making British Shoe Corporation, retail analysts said.
Sears' shares were being weighed down by the negative value ascribed to British Shoe Corporation and the price might recover if BSC was ditched, analysts said.

Strong, hired in 1992 to streamline Sears' hotch-potch of retail businesses, was seen under pressure to quit with institutional investors said to be losing patience and pressing for a management change.
Analysts' believed drastic action such as demerging Sears' profitable Selfridges department store was long overdue, but were uncertain whether the restructuring would go this far.
